contenido: 1. The human person, according to the data of contemporary science, is so marked by sexuality that it is a main part of the factors that characterize human life. Truly, in sex lie the characteristic notes that constitute people as men and women on the biological, psychological and spiritual level, thus having a large part in their individual evolution and their insertion into society. For this reason, as can easily be seen, sexuality is nowadays a topic frequently addressed in books, weeklies, magazines and other social media.

2. The Church cannot remain indifferent to such confusion of spirits and relaxation of customs. This is, in fact, a question of utmost importance for the personal life of Christians and for the social life of our time.

3. The men of our time are increasingly convinced that human dignity and vocation demand that, in the light of their intelligence, they discover the goods and potentialities inscribed in their own nature, that they develop them ceaselessly and that they realize them in their lives for ever greater progress.

4. Those are mistaken, therefore, who now maintain in large numbers that, to serve as a rule for particular actions, no absolute and immutable norm can be found neither in human nature nor in the revealed law, other than that which is expressed in the general law of charity and respect for human dignity. As proof of this assertion, they add that, in what we call norms of natural law or precepts of Holy Scripture, we should only see forms of a particular culture, expressed at a certain moment in history.

5. Since sexual ethics refers to certain fundamental goods of human life and Christian life, this general doctrine applies in the same way. In this field there are principles and norms that the Church has always transmitted in its teaching without the slightest doubt, even if the opinions and customs of the world opposed them. These principles and these norms do not in any way owe their origin to a particular type of culture, but to the knowledge of divine law and human nature. Therefore, they cannot be considered outdated, nor can they be questioned under the pretext of a new cultural situation.

6. The present declaration is not intended to deal with all abuses of the sexual faculty, nor with everything that the practice of chastity implies, but rather to recall the judgment of the Church on certain particular points, given the urgent need to oppose serious errors and widely disseminated norms of aberrant behavior.

7. Many today claim the right to sexual union before marriage, at least when a firm resolution to contract it and an affection that in a certain way is already conjugal in the minds of the couple ask for this complement, which they judge to be connatural; especially when the celebration of marriage is prevented by circumstances, or when this intimate relationship seems necessary for the preservation of love.

8. In our days—based on psychological observations—some have come to judge leniently, and even completely excuse, relationships between people of the same sex, against the constant doctrine of the Magisterium and against the moral sense of the Christian people.

9. Today the traditional doctrine according to which masturbation constitutes a serious moral disorder is frequently questioned or expressly denied. It is said that psychology and sociology demonstrate that this is a normal phenomenon in the evolution of sexuality, especially in adolescents, and that true guilt is not given except to the extent that the subject deliberately gives in to a self-satisfaction closed in on itself (ipsación); So yes, the act is radically contrary to the loving union between people of different sexes, such union being, in the opinion of some, the main objective of the use of the sexual faculty.

10. Respect for the moral law in the field of sexuality, as well as the practice of chastity, are compromised to no small extent, especially among less fervent Christians, by the current tendency to reduce to the extreme, at least in the concrete existence of men, the reality of serious sin, if not even to deny it.

11. As stated above, this declaration is intended to draw the attention of the faithful, in the current circumstances, to certain moral errors and disorders from which they must guard. But the virtue of chastity is not limited to avoiding the indicated faults. It also has other positive and higher demands. It is a virtue that marks the entire personality in its behavior, both internal and external.

12. The apostle Saint Paul describes in pathetic terms the painful conflict that man, a servant of sin, experiences internally between the law of his mind and the law of the flesh in his members, which holds him captive. But man can achieve deliverance from his “body of death” by the grace of Jesus Christ. This grace is enjoyed by the men whom she herself has justified, those whom the law of the spirit of life in Christ freed from the law of sin and death. That is why the Apostle conjures them: "Let sin no longer reign in your mortal body, subject to its lusts."

13. It is up to the bishops to teach the faithful the moral doctrine that refers to sexuality, whatever the difficulties that the fulfillment of this duty may encounter in the ideas and customs that are widespread today. This traditional doctrine must be deepened, expressed in a manner suitable to clarify consciences in the face of new situations, enriched with the discernment of what is true and useful that can be said about the meaning and value of human sexuality. But the principles and standards of moral life reaffirmed in this declaration must be faithfully maintained and taught. In particular, an attempt will be made to make the faithful understand that the Church preserves them not as inveterate traditions that are maintained superstitiously (tabús), nor by virtue of Manichaean prejudices, as is often repeated, but because it knows with certainty that they correspond to the divine order of creation and the spirit of Christ, and, consequently, also to human dignity.
